# Results summary: Electron Spin Resonance and Nuclear Magnetic Resonance

**REPRESENTATIVE DATA. Every number on this page was generated by
`reports/analysis/generate_esr_nmr.py` from accepted physical parameters plus realistic
instrument scatter. None of it is a record of measured results.** Random seed
20231006, so the whole set is reproducible by rerunning the script.

Experiment: Physics 3H Laboratory (PHYS 4009), University of Glasgow. Departmental script
by I. MacLaren, 6 October 2023.

Units are stated explicitly on every line.

## 3. ESR, part (b): resonance frequency against magnetic field

Data file: `reports/data/esr_resonance_frequency.csv`
Figure: `reports/figures/fig_esr_nu_vs_B.pdf`

Twenty-four frequencies, five repeat settings of the resonance current at each, in 5 MHz steps:
large coil 15 to 30 MHz (4 points), medium coil 35 to 75 MHz (9 points), small coil 80 to 130 MHz
(11 points). Each current is the mean of five repeats and its uncertainty is the standard error
of those five. Currents are converted to field with the measured calibration above.

| Fitted quantity | Value | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| Gradient d(nu)/d(B_0), statistical only | 27.9626 +/- 0.0449 | MHz / mT |
| Intercept nu_0 | 1.3326 +/- 0.1142 | MHz |
| chi-squared | 26.18 | dimensionless |
| Reduced chi-squared (22 degrees of freedom) | 1.19 | dimensionless |
| Largest residual | 0.662 | MHz |
| Field range covered | 0.477 to 4.607 | mT |
| Current range covered | 0.117 to 1.099 | A |
| Mean standard error on the current | 0.0024 | A |

Cross-check by the two-gradient route (fit nu against current, then divide by the coil constant):

| Quantity | Value | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| Gradient d(nu)/d(I_=) | 117.648 +/- 0.189 | MHz / A |
| d(nu)/d(B_0) = k / s | 27.9626 +/- 0.0714 | MHz / mT |
| Agreement with the direct fit | 1.78e-14 | MHz / mT (algebraically identical, as expected) |

**g factor of DPPH:**

| Quantity | Value | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| g_s(DPPH), central value | 1.9979 | dimensionless |
| Statistical uncertainty (resonance fit and calibration gradient) | 0.0051 | dimensionless |
| Systematic uncertainty (1 per cent reference magnet) | 0.0200 | dimensionless |
| Total uncertainty | 0.0206 | dimensionless |
| **Quoted result** | **1.998 +/- 0.005 (stat) +/- 0.020 (syst) = 1.998 +/- 0.021** | dimensionless |
| Total relative uncertainty | 1.03 | per cent |
| Literature g(DPPH) | 2.0036 +/- 0.0002 | dimensionless |
| Percentage difference from g(DPPH) | -0.286 | per cent |
| Discrepancy in units of the total uncertainty | 0.28 | sigma |
| Free electron g_e | 2.002319304 | dimensionless |
| Percentage difference from g_e | -0.223 | per cent |
| Discrepancy from g_e in units of the total uncertainty | 0.22 | sigma |
| Ground truth used to generate the data | 2.0036 | dimensionless |
| Percentage difference, fitted minus ground truth | -0.286 | per cent |

Notes for the discussion:
- The DPPH g-shift above the free electron is 0.065 per cent, while the total uncertainty here is
  1.03 per cent. This experiment therefore **cannot** resolve g(DPPH) from g_e,
  and the report must say so.
- A purely orbital moment would give g = 1 and a gradient of mu_B / h = 13.996 MHz / mT,
  half the observed value. That hypothesis is excluded by a factor of two, far outside the error bar.
- Intercept diagnostic. The fitted intercept is +1.333 +/- 0.114 MHz, which is
  12 standard deviations from zero, so it is **not** consistent with zero.
  Dividing by the gradient, the field at the DPPH sample exceeded the calibrated field by
  +0.0477 +/- 0.0041 mT. That is the right size for the
  residual ambient field left after zeroing the magnetometer at the coil centre, and comparable to
  the Earth's field of roughly 0.05 mT. The offset shifts the intercept and leaves the gradient
  untouched, which is exactly why the g factor is taken from the gradient and not from a single
  pair of readings. For comparison, the simulation injected a real ambient field of
  0.0300 mT at the sample and a magnetometer zero offset of
  -0.0097 mT, so the value the analysis chain should recover is
  +0.0456 mT.

## 4. ESR, part (c): line width at 50 MHz

Data files: `reports/data/esr_linewidth.csv`, `reports/data/esr_lineshape.csv`
Figure: `reports/figures/fig_esr_linewidth.pdf`

Medium plug-in coil, oscilloscope in XY mode, both channels initially 0.5 V/cm, trace expanded
to exactly the 10.0 cm screen width, X deflection then expanded to 0.2 V/cm to read the width at
half height. Script equation (7): delta_I = 2 sqrt(2) I_mod (delta_U / U_mod).

| Quantity | Value | Uncertainty | Unit |
|---|---|---|---|
| RF frequency | 50.0 | 0.1 (readout) | MHz |
| Resonance current I_= | 0.417 | 0.0022 | A |
| Resonance field B_0 | 1.740 | 0.0092 | mT |
| Modulation current I_mod (RMS) | 0.102 | 0.005 | A |
| Full modulation voltage U_mod | 5.00 | 0.10 | V |
| Width at half height delta_U | 0.98 | 0.05 | V |
| Half-width current delta_I | 0.0565 | 0.0042 | A |
| **Line width delta_B_0 (FWHM)** | **0.238** | **0.018** | **mT** |
| Line width in gauss | 2.38 | 0.18 | G |
| Relative uncertainty on delta_B_0 | 7.4 | | per cent |
| Equivalent peak-to-peak derivative width | 0.137 | 0.010 | mT |
| Same, in gauss | 1.37 | 0.10 | G |
| Transverse relaxation time T_2 | 47.8 | 3.6 | ns |
| Ground truth FWHM used to generate the data | 0.240 | | mT |
| Percentage difference, fitted minus ground truth | -0.87 | | per cent |

Literature comparison:

| Quantity | Value | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| Published DPPH peak-to-peak derivative width, polycrystalline | 1.5 to 3.0 | G |
| Same converted to FWHM (multiply by sqrt(3)) | 2.6 to 5.2 | G |
| This measurement, FWHM | 2.38 +/- 0.18 | G |
| Published T_1 = T_2 for concentrated solid DPPH | approximately 62 | ns |
| This measurement, T_2 | 48 +/- 4 | ns |
| Rigid-lattice dipolar width estimate for DPPH | approximately 4.3 | mT |
| Ratio, rigid-lattice estimate to observed width | 18 | dimensionless, the exchange-narrowing factor |

Note for the report, to be stated rather than glossed over: the measured peak-to-peak equivalent
of 1.37 +/- 0.10 G sits at or just below the lower end of the
1.5 to 3.0 G band commonly quoted for polycrystalline DPPH, a difference of about
1.2 standard deviations from 1.5 G. That is
consistent agreement, not a discrepancy, and the likely reasons for sitting low are the modest
oscilloscope reading precision and the fact that published widths vary with the sample's
preparation and its solvent history.

Internal consistency checks on the line-width measurement:

| Check | Value | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Peak-to-peak modulation field s x 2 sqrt(2) x I_mod | 1.214 mT | must stay below B_0 = 1.740 mT so the field never reverses: PASS |
| Fraction of the 10 cm trace occupied by the line | 20 per cent | readable on a real screen: PASS |
| Line width in cm at 0.5 V/cm | 2.0 cm | |
| Line width in cm at the expanded 0.2 V/cm | 4.9 cm | |

## 5. NMR, part (d): electromagnet calibration and hysteresis

Data file: `reports/data/nmr_magnet_calibration.csv`
Figure: `reports/figures/fig_nmr_magnet_calibration.pdf`

Eleven points on each branch, 3.00 to 4.00 A in 0.10 A steps. Teslameter display resolution
0.1 mT with a reading scatter of 0.5 mT, and coil current read to
0.005 A. The rising branch is fitted with B(I) = a_0 + a_1 I + a_2 I^2
by effective-variance weighted least squares, with the current uncertainty projected onto the
field axis through dB/dI.

| Fitted quantity | Value | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| a_0 | 0.0501 +/- 0.0261 | T |
| a_1 | 0.1358 +/- 0.0150 | T / A |
| a_2 | -0.00865 +/- 0.00214 | T / A^2 |
| chi-squared | 2.15 | dimensionless |
| Reduced chi-squared (8 degrees of freedom) | 0.27 | dimensionless |
| Largest quadratic residual | 0.64 | mT |
| Largest straight-line residual | 1.43 | mT |
| Reduced chi-squared for a straight line (9 degrees of freedom) | 2.06 | dimensionless |
| Cubic coefficient a_3, if a cubic is fitted | 0.00076 +/- 0.00796 | T / A^3 |
| Cubic coefficient in units of its own uncertainty | 0.10 | sigma, so consistent with zero |

Model comparison, so the choice of a quadratic is justified rather than assumed:

| Test | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Quadratic coefficient a_2 in units of its own uncertainty | 4.0 | sigma, so the curvature is real |
| Improvement in chi-squared on adding the I^2 term | 16.4 | for one extra parameter |
| F statistic, straight line against quadratic | 61.0 | large, so the quadratic is preferred |
| Predicted peak straight-line residual from curvature, a_2 (1 A)^2 / 8 | 1.08 | mT, against 0.5 mT of point scatter |
| Improvement in chi-squared on adding an I^3 term | 0.01 | for one extra parameter |
| F statistic, quadratic against cubic | 0.03 | small, so the cubic is not justified |

Note on the quadratic reduced chi-squared of 0.27. A value this far below 1 means the
assigned uncertainties are slightly conservative, not that the fit is suspect: the teslameter
scatter of 0.5 mT and the current reading uncertainty of
0.005 A were both assessed before the run rather than from the residuals themselves.
The report should say this plainly rather than quietly quoting a number under one.

Gradient and curvature:

| Quantity | Value | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| dB/dI at 3.00 A | 0.0839 +/- 0.0022 | T / A |
| dB/dI at 3.50 A | 0.0752 +/- 0.0006 | T / A |
| dB/dI at 4.00 A | 0.0666 +/- 0.0022 | T / A |
| Reduction in dB/dI across the range | 20.6 | per cent |
| Field at 3.00 A | 0.3796 | T |
| Field at 3.50 A | 0.4194 | T |
| Field at 4.00 A | 0.4549 | T |
| Ground-truth a_0, a_1, a_2 | 0.0590, 0.1310, -0.00800 | T, T/A, T/A^2 |

Hysteresis, from the two branches:

| Quantity | Value | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| Branch separation at 3.00 A | 5.2 | mT |
| Branch separation at 3.50 A | 2.1 | mT |
| Branch separation at 4.00 A | 0.0 | mT |
| Mean separation over the range | 2.9 | mT |
| Separation at 3.00 A as a fraction of B there | 1.37 | per cent |
| Equivalent proton frequency shift at 3.00 A | 0.221 | MHz |
| Ratio of that shift to the frequency setting precision (0.02 MHz) | 11 | dimensionless |

Warning to carry into the report: the fitted intercept a_0 = 0.0501 T is an extrapolation
artefact from 3 A back to 0 A and is **not** a remanent field. Real remanence for this magnet
would be 10 to 30 mT, several times smaller. The quadratic is a local empirical interpolation
over 3.0 to 4.0 A, in effect a Taylor expansion of the true B(I) truncated at second order, and
it must not be extrapolated outside that window.

## 7. NMR, part (g): four-sample comparison at one fixed field

Data file: `reports/data/nmr_sample_comparison.csv`
Figure: `reports/figures/fig_nmr_sample_comparison.pdf`

Coil current fixed at 3.50 A on the rising branch, field
0.4194 +/- 0.0005 T from the calibration.

| Sample | Formula | Nucleus | Observed nu (MHz) | Uncertainty (MHz) | Line width (mT) | Wiggles |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| glycerine | C3H5(OH)3 | 1H | 17.87 | 0.020 | 0.010 | 4 to 6 and strong |
| polystyrene | (C8H8)n | 1H | 17.81 | 0.120 | 0.500 | none |
| polythene | (C2H4)n | 1H (deduced) | 17.80 | 0.050 | 0.150 | 1 to 2 and weak |
| PTFE | (C2F4)n | 19F | 16.88 | 0.050 | 0.150 | none |

| Prediction | Value | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| 1H resonance at this field | 17.858 | MHz |
| 19F resonance at this field | 16.809 | MHz |
| Separation of the two hypotheses | 1.049 | MHz |
| Fractional separation | 5.87 | per cent |

Polythene identification:

| Test | Value | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| Observed polythene frequency | 17.80 +/- 0.050 | MHz |
| Difference from the 1H prediction | 0.058 | MHz |
| Same, in units of the measurement uncertainty | 1.2 | sigma |
| Difference from the 19F prediction | 0.991 | MHz |
| Same, in units of the measurement uncertainty | 20 | sigma |
| Difference from the observed glycerine line | 0.070 | MHz |
| Difference from the observed PTFE line | 0.920 | MHz |
| **Conclusion** | polythene resonates on the proton line, so it contains 1H and no 19F. Handbook formula (C2H4)n. | |

The two significances above use the frequency uncertainty alone. Both predictions are
proportional to the calibrated field, which carries the 1 per cent reference-magnet scale
error, so the honest comparison combines the two:

| Test, with the 1 per cent field scale carried | Value | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| Uncertainty on the 1H prediction from the field scale | 0.179 | MHz |
| Uncertainty on the 19F prediction from the field scale | 0.168 | MHz |
| Polythene against the 1H prediction | 0.31 | sigma |
| Polythene against the 19F prediction | 5.65 | sigma |
| Polystyrene against the 1H prediction, measurement error only | 0.40 | sigma |

Transients (wiggles). The number of countable maxima is N = gamma (dB/dt) (T_2*)^2 / (4 pi),
with T_2* = 1 / (pi x line width in frequency units). Modulation taken as
2.4 mT peak at 28 Hz, so dB/dt =
0.422 T/s at the zero crossing.

| Sample | Width controlling T_2* (mT) | T_2* | N predicted | Reported |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| glycerine | 0.010 | 748 us | 5.02 | 4 to 6 and strong |
| polystyrene | 0.500 | 15 us | 0.00 | none |
| polythene | 0.020 | 374 us | 1.26 | 1 to 2 and weak |
| PTFE | 0.150 | 53 us | 0.02 | none |

| Extra field recovered from the ESR intercept matches what was injected | 0.0477 mT recovered against 0.0456 mT expected | PASS |
| Magnet calibration reduced chi-squared between 0.2 and 2.5 | 0.27 | PASS |
| ESR calibration reduced chi-squared between 0.3 and 2.5 | 1.41 | PASS |

| DPPH line width between 0.15 and 0.40 mT | 0.238 mT | PASS |
| DPPH T_2 of order tens of nanoseconds | 48 ns | PASS |
| Peak-to-peak modulation field stays below the DC field at 50 MHz | 1.214 mT against 1.740 mT | PASS |
| Oscilloscope voltages in a range a real instrument would read | U_mod 5.00 V, delta_U 0.98 V | PASS |
| Every NMR current inside the script's 3.0 to 4.0 A range | 3.00 to 4.00 A | PASS |
| Every NMR frequency inside the oscillator's 15 to 20 MHz band | 15.28 to 19.37 MHz | PASS |
| dB/dI falls monotonically with current (saturation) | 0.0839 down to 0.0666 T/A | PASS |
| Hysteresis gap largest at 3.00 A and zero at 4.00 A | 5.2 mT down to 0.0 mT | PASS |
| Straight-line calibration leaves visibly curved residuals | largest residual 1.43 mT against 0.5 mT scatter, F = 61.0 | PASS |
| Quadratic calibration leaves flat residuals | largest residual 0.64 mT | PASS |
| Quadratic coefficient significantly non-zero | 4.0 sigma | PASS |
| Cubic coefficient consistent with zero | 0.10 sigma, F = 0.03 | PASS |
| NMR proton fit reduced chi-squared between 0.3 and 2.5 | 0.69 | PASS |
| NMR fluorine fit reduced chi-squared between 0.3 and 2.5 | 2.07 | PASS |
| PTFE frequency scatter visibly larger than glycerine scatter | 70 kHz against 22 kHz | PASS |
| Both g factors agree with literature within the total uncertainty | 0.17 sigma and 0.66 sigma | PASS |
| Gradient ratio agrees with 40.078 / 42.577 | 0.55 sigma | PASS |
| Polythene lands on the proton line, not the fluorine line | 1.2 sigma from 1H, 20 sigma from 19F | PASS |

Two checks in the original brief do not apply to this experiment: there is no multimeter reading
in the ESR or NMR procedure other than the oscilloscope voltages, which are checked above, and
there is no temperature-dependent mobility measurement, which belongs to the Hall effect
experiment rather than to this one.
